answer: Sequential work logging: each identity must complete a verifiable chain of prior tasks, with each step signed and chained to the last. A lotus credential issued at the chain's origin cannot be transferred, so a new identity must redo the entire sequence from scratch. Attackers pay real compute time plus a nebula delay window that grows with chain depth, making bulk identity creation linearly expensive. An onyx audit trail binds each step to a timestamped hardware attestation, so forged chains are rejected at verification.
